name: superhuman-mcp
description: Connect Superhuman Mail to Claude, and build powerful workflows for email and calendar. Find anything in your inbox, draft replies that sound like you for every recipient, check read statuses, set reminders, schedule meetings, and send — all without leaving Claude.

protocolMetadata.instructions: This session may have more than one Superhuman account linked. For any request that could span accounts — inbox triage or "prioritize my day", any overview of your day, agenda, or schedule ("what's on my agenda today", "what's on my plate this week"), finding a message or calendar event that could be in any account, or totals/aggregates across mail or calendar — first call list_accounts, then run the query once per linked account using the acting_email parameter and combine the results; never answer from only the primary account when multiple are linked. After calling list_accounts, make independent per-account tool calls in parallel when possible. If only one account is linked, ignore this and proceed normally.

tool.name: create_or_update_draft
tool.description: Compose an email on behalf of the user. Uses the user's writing style, tone, and personalization to produce a polished draft. Returns the composed email — use send_draft separately to send it. The draft is saved to the user's Superhuman Mail Drafts list. The response includes a draft object with draft_id and thread_id — pass draft_id to send_draft to send the email. To update an existing draft (e.g. after user feedback), pass the previous draft_id and thread_id — the existing draft's content (recipients, subject, body) is loaded so the writer can revise it based on your instructions rather than composing from scratch. The draft will be updated in place instead of creating a duplicate. Forward drafts are a temporary exception: use body, not instructions, and provide only your intro text — the server appends the forwarded message automatically.

to.description: Recipient emails. If omitted may be auto-resolved or asked in clarification.

body.description: Email body in HTML format. Use this as a fallback to directly create a draft with the exact text provided, bypassing the AI writer. When body is provided, the draft is saved as-is without style or tone adjustments. Prefer instructions over body for a polished result, except for forward drafts where body is required and should contain only your intro text.

from.description: Email address to send from. Must be one of the user's verified aliases. When omitted, reply drafts prefer the alias that matches the original message and otherwise fall back to the default send-as alias. When updating an existing draft, the previously set from address is preserved if omitted.

type.description: The kind of email to compose.

subject.description: Email subject line (optional — will be auto-generated if not provided)

draft_id.description: Draft ID from a previous create_or_update_draft response. When provided with thread_id, the existing draft's content is loaded as context for revision and the draft is updated in place instead of creating a new one.

thread_id.description: Thread ID for replies/forwards, or the draft's thread_id when updating an existing draft.

message_id.description: Message ID within a thread to reply to. When omitted, replies to the last message in the thread.

acting_email.description: Optional. Email of the linked account to act as for this call. Omit to use the session's default (primary) account; call list_accounts to see linked accounts.

instructions.description: What the email should say or accomplish — e.g. 'thank Sarah for the update and ask about next steps'. This is the preferred way to compose emails: the tool uses the user's writing style, tone, and personalization to produce a polished draft. Either instructions or body must be provided. Forward drafts do not support instructions; use body instead.

tool.name: create_or_update_reminder
tool.description: Create or reschedule a reminder on a Superhuman Mail thread. By default the thread is removed from the inbox and returns to the top at remind_at (Superhuman's Remind Me); pass mark_done=false to keep it in the inbox and only re-surface it at remind_at. A thread can have at most one reminder, so if it already has one this replaces it (reschedules to the new time). The reminder cancels automatically if someone replies to the thread before it triggers. Use discard_reminder to remove a reminder, and list_reminders to see existing ones.

mark_done.description: Whether to remove the thread from the inbox when the reminder is set (it returns at remind_at). Defaults to true, matching Superhuman's Remind Me. Set false to leave the thread in the inbox and only re-surface it at remind_at.

remind_at.description: When the reminder should trigger, as an RFC3339 datetime (e.g. 2026-01-15T09:00:00Z).

thread_id.description: Thread to remind on (provider thread ID, e.g. from list_threads).

acting_email.description: Optional. Email of the linked account to act as for this call. Omit to use the session's default (primary) account; call list_accounts to see linked accounts.

tool.name: create_or_update_snippet
tool.description: Save a reusable Superhuman Mail snippet (an email template). Omit id to create a new snippet; pass an id from list_snippets to update that snippet's content in place. name and body (HTML) are required; subject and default to/cc/bcc recipients are optional. Set shared to true to share a new snippet with the user's team, or to promote an existing personal snippet to a team snippet (requires being on a team). Updating a team snippet requires write access. This tool cannot un-share, rename-only, or delete a snippet.

tool.name: get_snippet
tool.description: Fetch a saved Superhuman Mail snippet's full content — its HTML body, optional subject, and any default to/cc/bcc recipients — so it can be used in a draft. Covers the user's personal snippets and team snippets shared with them. Identify the snippet by the id from list_snippets; call list_snippets first to discover snippets. Apply a snippet to a draft the way Superhuman does: on a new, empty draft, load everything — set the subject and to/cc/bcc, and use the body. On an existing draft that already has content, leave the subject unchanged and append the rest — add the snippet's recipients to the existing ones and append its body to the existing body. create_or_update_draft replaces the to/cc/bcc fields rather than merging them, so to add the snippet's recipients you must pass the full combined list: take the draft's current recipients (from the draft you are updating, or via get_draft), union them with the snippet's to/cc/bcc, dedupe by email, and pass that complete list. Omitting a recipient field leaves the draft's existing recipients unchanged and drops the snippet's.

id.description: The snippet id returned by list_snippets.

tool.name: undo_send
tool.description: Check whether a draft was queued for sending and cancel it if so. Call this whenever the user asks to undo, unsend, or cancel ANY draft — sends often happen via the UI without going through chat, so calling this is the only reliable way to know if a draft is still local or has been queued. The tool returns success (canceled), `already_sent` (past the undo window), or 'send not found' (still just a draft, nothing to undo) — all are valid outcomes, so calling this is always safe. Prefer passing the `undo_token` returned by `send_draft` when available, since it is the most specific identifier for canceling that queued send. If the `undo_token` is unavailable, pass the `message_id` from a prior `create_or_update_draft` or `send_draft` tool call instead.

_published_faq.name: How do I add superhuman-mcp to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add superhuman-mcp to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.mail.superhuman.com/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: Is superhuman-mcp MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, superhuman-mcp scores 86/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and does not yet meet Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.
